summary: This section explains how rules for meetings and resolutions are relaxed for a One Person Company. Instead of holding traditional meetings, a One Person Company can pass resolutions by writing them in a special book. This applies to both general meetings and board meetings when there is only one director.
points: Section 98 and sections 100 to 111 do not apply to a One Person Company.
Ordinary business meant for an annual general meeting is handled differently for a One Person Company.
A resolution for a One Person Company is valid if the member communicates it, enters it in the minutes-book, and signs and dates it.
The date on which the member signs the resolution is treated as the date of the meeting.
If there is only one director, a board resolution is valid if entered in the minutes-book, signed, and dated by that director.
example: Aarav is the sole member and the only director of Aarav Printing Private Limited, which is a One Person Company. When the company needs to pass an ordinary business matter or a resolution that other companies would vote on at a big meeting, Aarav does not need to arrange a formal gathering. Instead, Aarav writes down the decision, enters it into the official minutes-book, and signs and dates it. Under the law, the date Aarav signs this book is considered the official date of the meeting for all legal purposes.

terms.meaning: A company that has only one person as a member.
A formal decision or choice made by a member or director.
A book required by law used to record the official business and decisions of a company.

watch: People often confuse these relaxed rules for One Person Companies with the strict meeting requirements that apply to normal companies with multiple members.
